title: Data Engineer
desc: Shirley Ryan AbilityLab is the global leader in physical medicine and rehabilitation for adults and children with the most severe, complex conditions. By joining our team, you’ll be part of our life-changing mission and vision. You’ll contribute to an innovative, multifaceted culture that is second to none — one that embraces collaboration, excellence, discovery and compassion. You’ll play a role in something that’s never been done before as we integrate science and clinical care to help patients achieve better, faster outcomes — as we Advance Human Ability, together. Job Description Summary General Summary The Data Engineer is a member of the Data Platform Engineering team, working in a dynamic cross-functional environment to assist in developing the strategic direction and the meaningful use of data within the organization for our next generation data platform to provide a full and self-service environment for clinicians, researchers, administrators and executives. Assists with development or selection of data models to be implemented in support of clinical, quality improvement, and research objectives. Creates ETL pipelines for data to and from various cloud and local sources consistent with existing data models. Adapts database systems and architecture as necessary to meet the operational, analytical, and reporting needs of the organization. The Data Engineer will consistently demonstrate support of the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab statement of Vision, Mission and Core Values by striving for excellence, contributing to the team efforts and showing respect and compassion for patients and their families, fellow employees, and all others with whom there is contact at or in the interest of the institute. The Data Engineer will demonstrate Shirley Ryan AbilityLab Core Attributes: Communication, Accountability, Flexibility/Adaptability, Judgment/Problem Solving, Customer Service and Core Values (Hope, Compassion, Discovery, Collaboration, & Commitment to Excellence) while fulfilling job duties. Job Description The Data Engineer will: Collaborate within the Data Platform Engineering team, Data Analytics and Data Governance teams, other Information Services (IS) teams, executive leadership, external consultants, and stakeholders from various departments within the hospital to: Primarily utilizing existing resources, assist in developing secure, stable, scalable long-term plans for the flow of the hospital’s data. Assist in the development of scalable data infrastructure and platforms to collect and process large amounts of data, including structured and unstructured data for analysis by clinical, research, and business resources. Data sources may be internally (locally) or externally (cloud) sourced, both data owned by the organization and external to the organization from partners and vendors. Establish methods and procedures for tracking data quality, completeness, redundancy, compliance and improvement along with related system operational performance. Create strategies and plans for data capacity planning, data security, life cycle data management, scalability, backup and archiving. Create the mapping of data sources, data movement, interfaces, and analytics, with the goal of ensuring data quality and accurate downstream delivery and reporting. Define standards for engineering and architecture including naming, describing, managing, modeling, cleaning, enriching, transforming, transferring, storing, searching, and delivering data securely within the hospital. Assist with data stewardship by tagging and defining data elements in collaboration with subject matter experts and the Data Governance team. Participate in data structure and information model design across multiple stakeholders. Acquire and maintain data from primary or secondary data sources. Identify and evaluate opportunities for enhancement of current data architecture and data management technologies. Monitor, update, and ensure consistent uptime, availability and access of the data platform and other data systems for performance and reliability. Develop processes to support the deployment of high quality, flexible, and secure data management solutions Leverage available tools to drive Automation of key data management processes Create instrumentation and metrics to ensure ecosystem health & ensure continuous improvement of KPI’s ​Reporting Relationships Reports directly to the Director Data Platform Architecture Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Required Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science or computer engineering, or in a related area (data science, mathematics, statistics, economics, etc.) with demonstrated proficiency in the skills below. Expertise in SQL (5 years professional) with experience with MySQL, PostgreSQL and their derivatives in building complex queries, tuning, and optimization Expertise in Python and/or Java (5 years professional) with a focus on data manipulation, database interaction, ETL automation, big data technologies, and performance optimization Knowledge and understanding of HIPAA and ability to implement data security standards in line with those requirements including inter-operability with HL7 and FHIR. At least 2-5 years of professional experience establishing ETL/ELT processes for securely transporting data between cloud and local databases. Experience doing so between Snowflake, AWS RDS (Aurora), OCI, Microsoft Power Apps, and using Informatica is a plus. Experience with other AWS data utilities (API gateway, S3, etc.) is a plus. Demonstrated experience in handling large data sets and relational databases, data warehousing, scalability, reliability, access and provisioning. Experience evaluating and leveraging AI utilities in data warehouse and data governance tools for model and pipeline development while ensuring quality data for the analytics layer and self-services. Strong communication skills, particularly those relevant to translating highly technical information for non-technical audiences in terms of documentation and diagrams. Demonstrated ability to manage and see through long-term projects. Proactive work habits such as proposing and developing new projects and initiatives or advocating and promoting incremental adoption of new technologies. Candidates familiar with Oracle-Cerner EHR systems, particularly the Millennium data model and CCL, will receive strong consideration. Candidates familiar with research CDMs like OMOP, i2b2, and PCORnet will be strongly considered. Candidates with experience developing REST/RESTful APIs, streaming platforms, and role-based access and encryption will also be strongly considered. Working Conditions Normal office environment with little or no exposure to dust or extreme temperature. title: Data Engineer
desc: The Data Engineer is responsible for designing, building, and maintaining the company’s data infrastructure — from raw data ingestion through to production-ready datasets that serve both operational systems and AI workloads. A core focus of this role is building a comprehensive metadata and semantic layer that clearly describes every dataset, table, and field, enabling AI systems to scan, analyze, and generate reports autonomously. This role works closely with the technical team, AI team, project team, and clients to ensure data is reliable, well-documented, and ready for both human analysis and machine consumption. Job Description: The Role Data Pipeline Development Design and build automated ETL/ELT pipelines to ingest data from multiple sources (Call Center, DMS, Social Platform, third-party APIs). Develop scheduling, monitoring, and alerting mechanisms to ensure pipeline reliability and SLA compliance. Implement incremental processing, deduplication, and change data capture (CDC) strategies for high-volume data flows. Maintain and optimize existing pipelines for performance, cost, and maintainability. Metadata & Semantic Layer Build and maintain a comprehensive metadata catalog with clear descriptions for every table and column across all datasets. Design and implement a semantic layer that defines dataset purposes, field definitions, data types, business logic, and relationships between tables. Ensure the semantic layer is structured for AI consumption — enabling AI systems to understand data context, scan datasets, perform analysis, and generate reports without manual intervention. Establish and enforce documentation standards so that every new dataset or schema change is accompanied by complete metadata. Collaborate with the AI team to validate that the semantic layer provides sufficient context for automated data exploration and insight generation. Data Quality & Governance Implement automated data quality checks at each pipeline stage: completeness, accuracy, consistency, and freshness. Build monitoring dashboards to track data health metrics and alert on anomalies or pipeline failures. Establish data lineage tracking so that downstream consumers (reports, dashboards, AI models) can trace data to its source. Collaborate with stakeholders to define data ownership, access policies, and retention rules. AI Data Infrastructure Prepare and serve datasets for AI/ML workloads: feature stores, training datasets, and inference data feeds. Collaborate with the AI team to define data requirements for model training, evaluation, and monitoring. Build and maintain data APIs or serving layers that enable AI systems to consume data in real time or near-real time. Support the AI team in data profiling, exploratory analysis, and data readiness assessments for new AI use cases. Cross-team Collaboration Work with the technical team on system integration and data flow architecture across platforms. Collaborate with the AI team to ensure data infrastructure meets the requirements of AI/ML workloads. Support the project team and clients in understanding data availability, structure, and operational workflows. Participate in client-facing discussions to gather data requirements and provide technical guidance on data solutions. Location: Ho Chi Minh City Brand: Merkle Time Type: Full time Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract (Fixed Term)

title: Wealth Management - Fiduciary Consulting Group (FCG), Performance Analyst - Analyst / Associate
location: Greenwood Village, Colorado, United States of America
desc: Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. Morgan Stanley Wealth Management (MSWM) has over $2 trillion under management and is one of the world’s largest networks of Financial Advisors. The Fiduciary Consulting Group at Morgan Stanley (“FCG”) is the Institutional RIA business, which consults on over $200 billion of institutional assets. The Institutional RIA business was launched in 2021 through the acquisitions of Hyas Group and Cook Street Consulting and subsequently the Southern Employee Benefits practice of Milliman. Its goal is to continue strategic acquisitions in this space and help support organic growth. The business is a high priority strategic initiative within Morgan Stanley to increase market share within the institutional consulting market while also contributing to the Firm’s asset growth and participant engagement goals. We currently seek a full-time entry level Performance Analyst to begin work immediately in our Greenwood Village, Colorado office. *PLEASE INCLUDE COVER LETTER EXPLAINING YOUR INTEREST IN A CAREER IN INVESTMENT CONSULTING/FINANCE AND SKILL SETS APPLICABLE TO THE POSITION* The individual selected for this position will be responsible for ongoing investment due diligence, analysis and reporting to institutional clients, specifically to include: Direct client & consultant support Client performance reporting Data integration & reconciliation with outside parties Recordkeeping and investment expense evaluation & benchmarking* Client vendor management Asset class, macroeconomic, and industry research FCG’s Performance Reporting Department is responsible for supporting our consultants with client relationships. We are looking for an ambitious individual who is interested in a long-term career in the investment consulting industry. Qualifications: We welcome candidates from a variety of backgrounds. The following is a basic outline of desired qualities: Attentive to Detail – Our success as a firm is intrinsically linked to the quality and accuracy of our materials. Team-Oriented – Cooperation with the performance reporting, research, and consulting teams to meet deadlines with quality work is absolutely essential. Independent Thinker – A successful candidate must be capable of thinking critically and independently. A candidate must be able to quickly process new information and work autonomously under tight deadlines. Professional and Personable – The vast majority of our new business comes through referrals. Our reputation is one of the greatest assets we possess. A successful candidate must be comfortable interacting and presenting in different environments, such as with clients and investment managers. Ambitious – As part of Morgan Stanley's Fiduciary Consulting Group, we continue to grow and expand our capabilities. We are seeking an individual with a long-term interest in contributing to our team's continued success. Experience and Skill Set: Undergraduate degree required. Applicants with a strong interest in pursuing a career in the financial services industry, regardless of educational background, are encouraged to apply. Ideal candidate for this position will have 0-5 years of previous experience in a similar role within the investment or consulting industry. Strong written and verbal communication skills. The candidate will be proficient in Microsoft Office products (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook) Experience with investment and financial analysis platforms such as Bloomberg, eVestment, and Morningstar Direct is preferred Desire to progress towards the Chartered Financial Analyst® designation (if it has not already been attained). Ability to work 40 + hours when business needs dictate WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY: At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work. To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices​ into your browser. Salary range for the position: $57,000 and $110,000 per year. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary incentive compensation award. The successful candidate may be eligible to participate in the relevant business unit’s incentive compensation plan, which also may include a discretionary bonus component. Morgan Stanley offers a full spectrum of benefits, including Medical, Prescription Drug, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Account, Dependent Day Care Savings Account, Life Insurance, Disability and Other Insurance Plans, Paid Time Off (including Sick Leave consistent with state and local law, Parental Leave and 20 Vacation Days annually), 10 Paid Holidays, 401(k), and Short/Long Term Disability, in addition to other special perks reserved for our employees. Please visit mybenefits.morganstanley.com to learn more about our benefit offerings.
